about: Note scripts rendered by engines/build/fm1-render, by the app layer natively (tests/test_sim_web.py) and by the WebAssembly module under Node (sim/web/test/parity.mjs). Fields map to fm1-render's options; every engine and effect appears at least once. `cmd` is a sequencer verb script (fm1-render --cmd), relative to this file, at 64-frame blocks (#! block=64); it routes tracks with `route` verbs only, so track 0 plays the engine by the default-route rule. `panel` is panel input (fm1-sim-render --panel): the render legs then play what the native harness logged (--log-cmds and its sidecar of arguments, which starts with --slots, with the modulation's .mod log) instead of `cmd`. The app always runs four sound units and the default modulation rack; `sounds`, `inserts`, `levels` and `sound_notes` load and play the other units (fm1-render's multi-sound flags, which imply --slots). `mod` is a modulation script (fm1-render --mod, relative to this file). `sysex` is a .syx file of DX7 voices loaded into FM6's user bank first (fm1-render --sysex; the module's fm1w_dx7_load), relative to this file.

scenarios.name: dx7-macros-patches-steal
scenarios.why: FM6 (msfa): BRASS past the twelve-voice cap, the four macros turned while it sounds (Brightness, Env Time, Feedback, Volume on page 2), then Patch to VIBES, whose LFO amplitude modulation is the engine's own code.

scenarios.name: dx7-loop-lfo-pitch-env
scenarios.why: FM6: SAW BASS on algorithm 4 with its feedback loop (src/dx7_loop.cc), then STRINGS (LFO vibrato after a delay), KICK (the pitch envelope) and HI-HAT (fixed frequencies, feedback 7).

scenarios.name: dx7-user-bank
scenarios.why: FM6's user bank: the original test bank (tools/dx7_bank.py --test-bank) loaded into the module through fm1w_dx7_load as fm1-render --sysex loads it, then User 2, User 7 and User 32 played (the bank's algorithms 2, 7 and 32), unpacked by msfa's UnpackPatch.

scenarios.name: sophie-kit
scenarios.why: Sophie's feedback FM runs sinf/expf every sample; glibc's and musl's last-bit differences grow through the loop. A static musl build of fm1-render renders this byte for byte like the WebAssembly one (build-on-aeon.sh).

scenarios.name: sophie-clap-no-feedback
scenarios.why: Even without feedback, Sophie's envelopes and sweeps come from expf/exp2f/powf per voice and sinf per sample; a last-bit difference moves a clap burst by a sample. Identical to static musl.

scenarios.name: drums-deep-groove
scenarios.why: Drums (engines/src/drums.cc): the Deep kit's pads with a closed hat choking the open one, toms, a crash, velocities; the snare's Tone, Decay and Snap turned while it rings (Pad focuses it), the kit's Volume and Accent turned, a bend.

scenarios.name: drums-punch-models
scenarios.why: Drums: the Punch kit (the synthetic kick and snare, the ring-modulated hats), a cowbell on pad 13 by its Model, Drive and Sweep turned on the kick while it rings, the square-wave Hat on the open hat's pad (still choked by the closed one), the Deep kit chosen mid-run (the next hits take it), Accent up and the open hat's Decay down.

scenarios.name: drums-full-kit-steals
scenarios.why: Drums with every voice busy: all sixteen pads within 0.3 s, six of them ringing long, so steals take the quietest hit (the level each voice holds decides, a float comparison the browser must make as the desktop does); a closed hat with every voice busy takes the open hat's voice; then more hits steal again.

scenarios.name: seq-capture-stopped-capsel
scenarios.why: Capture's stopped tempo search scores each candidate tempo with logf (seq_capture.c); a last-bit difference between glibc's logf and musl's could reorder near-tied candidates and so the take. Identical to static musl and to fm1-render.js.

scenarios.name: api-v3-test-ext-transport
scenarios.why: Engine API v3's effect extension: Test Ext hears the sequencer's Start, beats (132 BPM, off the block grid) and Stop through fm1_fx_render in the app as in fm1-render, and the tempo (Probe); Comb after it.

scenarios.name: mod-log-keytrack
scenarios.why: Engine API v3's LOG law under modulation: NOTE at +100 % keytracks the Filter's Cutoff (the octave rule) while an LFO moves it and Echo's Time in octaves; a knob turn moves Cutoff's base under the routes. fm1_exp2f, so the module computes the same bits.

scenarios.name: mod-macro-routes
scenarios.why: Modulation (docs/16 MG3) from a script: cables into the sound, both effects, HOST PITCH and AMP at once, a chain of modules, a gate cable at 70 %, edits at 0.5 s and 0.8 s; the module plays the file through fm1w_mod_reset and fm1w_mod_text, the native legs through --mod.

scenarios.name: mod-panel-gestures
scenarios.why: Modulation made on the panel (docs/16 MG3): the routing gesture on HOME and FX, knobs in RACK, two cables from MATRIX, ending on MATRIX. The render legs replay what the native harness logged, the modulation included (its .mod log, named in the sidecar).

scenarios.name: seq-panel-play-stop
scenarios.why: The panel drives the sequencer (docs/15 S3): the module presses the buttons and turns the encoders; the render legs replay the commands and knob turns the native harness logged (--log-cmds and its .args sidecar), so this is also two-step parity.

scenarios.name: seq-panel-step-entry
scenarios.why: Step entry from the panel (docs/15 S4): taps with a chord from MIDI IN, a probability, a condition and an invert on the Step pages, a second bar, a nudge, a pitch added with SHIFT and a step cleared with a SHIFT tap, then two passes of the two-bar clip. The render legs replay what the native harness logged (--log-cmds and its .args sidecar, with the MIDI IN notes); the module presses the same keys and buttons and plays the same notes.

scenarios.name: seq-panel-record
scenarios.why: Record and Capture from the panel (docs/15 S5): REC with a bar's count-in and two keys recorded into the take, step record with a chord tied over two steps, a rest and a note at MIDI IN, then three keys captured while playing (SHIFT + REC). The keys' notes reach the sequencer as live input; the render legs replay them as the `non` and `nof` ops the native harness logged, with the keys' notes in its .args sidecar.

scenarios.name: seq-panel-capture-stopped
scenarios.why: A stopped Capture from the panel (docs/15 S5): six keys, then SHIFT + REC; the core reads the tempo, starts the transport and opens its picker, SELECT takes another tempo and a key closes it. The tempo search scores candidates with logf (seq_capture.c), as seq-capture-stopped-capsel; identical to static musl and to fm1-render.js.

scenarios.name: seq-metro-click
scenarios.why: The metronome's click (docs/15 S6, owner decision O11): a deterministic, integer-only click voice in the shared bridge (fm1_seq_click_mix), sounding each CLICK event while `metro` is on, added after the effects and before the limiter by fm1-render and the app alike: on while a bar plays, off, on again with swing, and a REC count-in after a stop.

scenarios.name: seq-panel-tracks
scenarios.why: Tracks from the panel (docs/15 S6): SEQ + a white key focuses track 2, its Track page routes it to Sound 2 (Shapes), MUTE held with a white key mutes track 4, the Set page sets swing and tempo, track 2's Clip page plays it at 1/2X and 2X, SHIFT + 6 turns the metronome's click on and off, and a MUTE tap mutes track 2. The render legs replay the harness's log (`watch`, `route`, `mute`, `swing`, `bpm`, `cscl`, `metro`) with --slots, so this is two-step parity across tracks and sound units.

scenarios.name: seq-panel-locks
scenarios.why: Parameter locks from the panel (docs/15 S8): a held step's lock page locks Timbre and Morph on step 5 and Harmonics on step 13 (`alabel`, `abase`, a quiet `aset`); playing, KNOB3 with no step held turns Timbre on its 7-bit grid and its lane's base follows (`abaseq`, and the knob's value replayed as --param-at); a stop just after step 5's locks sends each lane back to its base (D6), and PLAY plays on from there. The render legs replay the harness's log, so this is two-step parity for locks, base sync and the D6 revert.

scenarios.name: fx-turns-diffuse-psxverb
scenarios.why: Macro's 2-op FM through its ping LPG rather than Shapes' Pluck: since the lab switch went (2026-10-05) every chain plays under the RAM meter, which refuses Shapes beside Diffuse and PSX Verb.

scenarios.name: mod-multi-routes
scenarios.why: Modulation over several sound units (docs/16 MG3) from a script: cables into Sound 1, Sounds 2 and 4, an insert on each of them and both of Sound 2's, the master Plate and HOST AMP, with notes on three sounds and timed edits. The module plays the file through fm1w_mod_reset and fm1w_mod_text after loading the units, the native legs through fm1-render --slots --mod.

scenarios.name: mod-multi-panel
scenarios.why: Modulation over several sound units made on the panel (docs/16 MG3): with Sound 2 current, the gesture on HOME, on its insert and on the master, a MATRIX cable whose target picker opens at Sound 2, then a cable on Sound 1; tracks on both sounds, a key and a MIDI note. The render legs replay the harness's .mod log and sidecar through fm1-render --slots.

scenarios.name: mod-voice-routes
scenarios.why: Per-voice modulation (docs/16 MG9) from a script: an Envelope per note into Sound 1's Timbre with velocity per note shortening its attack, a random detune per note (the note's pitch), an LFO per note in trig mode into Sound 2's Color, Sound 2's notes alone gating ENV4 (S2RTRG) into Sound 2's pitch (PITCH2), an LFO on the current sound's pitch (PITCHC) moved by a `current` line, a re-struck held key, an edit and a per-voice cable switched off. The offsets reach Macro and Shapes through set_param_note; the module plays the file through fm1w_mod_reset and fm1w_mod_text, the native legs through fm1-render --slots --mod.

scenarios.name: multi-two-sounds-inserts
scenarios.why: Multi-sound (docs/15 §3.16): Macro as Sound 1 through a Crush insert at 80 %, Shapes as Sound 2 through Diffuse and Ensemble at 60 %, summed and through the master Comp (Plate until modulation's runtime, docs/16 MG3, began to count against the RAM budget, which Plate would now pass). Notes on each sound (--note on Sound 1, --sound-note on Sound 2); the render legs run fm1-render --slots with the same units.

scenarios.name: multi-four-sounds-seq
scenarios.why: Four tracks routed to four slots (`route t 1 k`, docs/15 §3.16): Macro, Shapes and Six-Op as Sounds 1, 2 and 4, Sound 3 empty, so track 2 plays nothing; each sound renders split at its own tracks' events (fm1_seq_host_dispatch_slots) through its own inserts and level, and each lock lane resolves on its own track's sound (Shapes' Color, Six-Op's Brightness, Macro's Timbre). The master is Ensemble rather than Plate since modulation (docs/16 MG3) counts its runtime against the RAM budget, which Plate would now pass.

scenarios.name: dyn3-squash-transient
scenarios.why: Dynamics pack 3 (2026-10-05): Squash through its three Types (each a Type change from the gain in force, crossfaded) with Snap's gate and Split under Squash 0.05 (blended to 1, pulled to rest), then Transient shaping the result; parity covers the ports' Newton square roots, quarter-sine and log/exp polynomials.

scenarios.name: dyn3-round-autogain
scenarios.why: Dynamics pack 3: Comp's loosened Auto Gain (only would-be overs touched, a Makeup cut counted) into the Limiter's Round mode (ClipOnly2 one frame ahead, no added delay), with Mode and Lookahead turned while it rounds.

scenarios.name: multi-panel
scenarios.why: Multi-sound from the panel (docs/15 §3.16): SHIFT + PRESETS makes Sound 2 current, a key and a MIDI IN note play it, KNOB2 turns its Timbre, the Mix page sets both levels, and SHIFT + PRESETS goes back to Sound 1, while two tracks play the two sounds. The render legs replay the harness's log and sidecar (--sound-note, --sound-param-at, --level-at), so this is two-step parity across sound units.
